# PR #4958: Patch: pin the perf corpus so card additions stop re-dealing it

Closes #4924

## What changed

`cargo jackioh perf` used to deal its 52 games from the live card pools on every run, so adding one card re-dealt every game it times. It now plays them from checked-in records in `crates/tools/perf-corpus/`, one JSON file per game. The games are plain golden seeds 1–40, handicapped 201–210, the run-start game and the Duos co-op game. Each record holds the game's kind, seed, catalog version and decks, plus its handicaps or deck marks where that kind has them.

- **`crates/tools/src/perf.rs`**
  - New record type `PerfRecord`, which refuses unknown fields, and its lint, modelled on the fuzz corpus:
    - a record may hold only its own kind's fields;
    - its catalog version must be a shipped one;
    - every deck id must be in the catalog unless the record is `retired`.
  - The corpus reader also rejects:
    - a live record of a game no `PERF_*` constant names;
    - a second live record of the same game;
    - a wanted game with no live record.
  - `play_seed`, `play_run_start` and `play_coop_game` take a record instead of dealing. The heaviest-state selection runs over the replayed games, as before.
  - New `perf --pin` is the only code that deals from the live pools. It writes a record for each game that lacks one, never rewrites a file (`File::create_new`), and writes nothing while the corpus has a problem.
  - `--json`'s `corpus` now lists `games` and `retired`, and the table's first line says `from N pinned games (M retired)`.
  - New constants: `PERF_RUN_START_SEED` (0), `PERF_COOP_SEED` (1) and `PERF_CORPUS_DIR`. No budget changed. The budget comment no longer says a card change re-measures the budgets.
- **`crates/tools/perf-corpus/`**: 52 records written by `perf --pin`, and a README covering the record shape, adding, retiring (the fuzz corpus's rule), running and scope.
- **`crates/tools/tests/perf.rs`**: the smoke test checks that `corpus.games` and `corpus.retired` match the live and retired files, and that each kind has a live record. Exit 0 with no failures shows every game replayed with no refused action.
- **`crates/tools/README.md`** (perf row and an example line) and **`docs/ADDING_CARDS.md`** §4 (a bullet on the perf corpus).

## How I tested it

- **Baseline before any edit**, `perf --smoke --json`: 77 states (40 hotseat, 2 wide, 15 plain, 15 handicapped, 3 run-start, 2 co-op), fold of seed 29 at 332 actions, duos fold 200 actions, `view_for bytes` median 7381.
- **Pinning:** `perf --pin` printed `perf --pin: 52 record(s) written`; a second run printed `0 record(s) written`.
- **Criterion 1 probe:** I temporarily set `POOL_EXCLUSIONS` in `fuzz.rs` to exclude `core-001`, which re-deals the live pools. `core-001` sits in the pinned decks of plain 11 and 34. Under the probe:
  - `--pin` wrote 0 records;
  - `perf --smoke --json` exited 0;
  - `sha256sum -c` over all 52 files passed;
  - `corpus.games` was unchanged.

  After restoring the line, `git diff --exit-code crates/tools/src/fuzz.rs` was clean. The before, after and probe reports reduced by `jq -S '{corpus: (.corpus|del(.games,.retired)), fold, duosFold}'` have the same sha256. So the pinned corpus is exactly the one `main` deals today.
- **Test results:**
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh perf::`: 16 passed, 8 of them new.
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test perf`: 1 passed, 1 ignored (the daily test).
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --features jackioh-engine/testkit --test acceptance`: 58 passed, including `readme_the_command_table_is_the_clis`.
- **The new unit tests cover:**
  - every deal lints clean and survives a save and reload;
  - the streams equal `spec_for_seed`'s;
  - a record dealt from a smaller pool plays its own decks and folds back to the same hash (criterion 1);
  - a removed id, in a 1v1 deck or a co-op seat, is told to add `"retired": "<which ids, which patch>"`, never edit its decks, and run `cargo jackioh perf --pin` (criterion 3);
  - each kind-field rule;
  - stray, duplicate and broken files;
  - `pin` never rewrites a file, and deals a retired game again as `…-2.json`;
  - the checked-in corpus holds exactly the wanted games.
- **Other checks:**
  - `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
  - `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
  - `catalog check`, `patches check` and `spec check`: ok.
  - `classify --base origin/main --claims`: `Internal`, so no patch fragment is needed.
- **Budgets:** `perf_holds_every_budget -- --ignored` ran once and passed, for example `reduce` 309.0 µs against 1,500 and `fold` 1,400.5 µs/action against 7,700. These numbers come from this machine, not GitHub's runners, so I changed no budget. The corpus is identical to `main`'s, so the medians measured for the budgets still apply.

## Where I departed from the plan

- `run_start_inputs()` returns a `PerfRecord` instead of a three-part tuple, and a small `unpinned()` helper builds an empty record. This avoids a complex tuple type.
- The plan's `streams` is named `golden_streams`, because only plain and handicapped games use those streams.
- `pin` writes with `File::create_new`, so the "never rewrites a file" promise holds even if the name check is wrong.
- I added a test the plan didn't list, for stray, duplicate and broken records.

## Worth a second look

- **Moved numbers:** the run-start setup values (35 health, 5 armor, 1 extra card, 1 mana) moved unchanged from `play_run_start` into `run_start_inputs`. They are not new numbers.
- **Duplicate records:** when two live records pin the same game, the error names the second in file-name order. `…-2.json` sorts before `….json`, so the unnumbered file is the one named.
- **CI scope:** as the plan said, I left `scripts/ci-scope.sh` alone. A change to `perf-corpus/*` therefore falls into the catch-all and turns on e2e smoke, though nothing e2e runs reads these files. Adding `crates/tools/perf-corpus/*` next to `crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/*` in the e2e skip list would save those minutes; it is left as a follow-up.
- **Accepted trade-off:** a new card joins no pinned game until records are dealt again. That is the point of the change, and the README's Scope section says so. In-game random pools (Discover and the like) still draw from the live catalog, so pinned games stay close rather than frozen.

# #4924: Patch: pin the perf corpus so card additions stop re-dealing it
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The engine-speed budgets the pull-request gate holds would stop wobbling every time cards ship. Today adding one card re-deals every game the perf corpus times, so medians jump for reasons that have nothing to do with the change under test, and someone has to re-measure the budgets by hand. After this change the corpus is a checked-in set of pinned games, so the same build always times the same games and a budget crossing means the code got slower.

## Why

`crates/tools/src/perf.rs` builds its corpus live on every run: plain golden seeds `PERF_SEED_FIRST..=PERF_SEED_LAST` (1..40), handicapped seeds 201..210, the heaviest states of each by the fuzz growth measures, one run-start game and one Duos game. The decks come from the live shipped pools (`spec_for_seed` in `crates/tools/src/golden.rs` deals from the shipped sets, via the fuzz deck streams), so any card addition re-deals the whole corpus. The file says so itself: between two corpora the 1v1 medians moved by up to 1.8x and the Duos ones by up to 5.6x, runner CPUs added another 1.3x, each time budget is 5x the largest of twelve medians, and a budget crossed by a card change that made the corpus heavier is measured again the same way (`perf.rs`, the budget comment). That re-measurement is pure upkeep, and the 5x headroom that absorbs corpus churn also dulls the budgets against real slowdowns. `crates/tools/tests/perf.rs` already pins the corpus shape (hotseat states, 2 wide boards, at least one plain, handicapped, run-start and co-op game), so a pinned corpus has a test waiting for it. The repo already knows how to pin deals: `crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/` keeps each kept failure's decks and start inputs literally, with a `retired` marker when a patch removes an id.

## Proposal

Check in the corpus inputs (seed, decks, handicaps, deck marks) for the plain range, the handicap range, the run-start game and the Duos game under `crates/tools/perf-corpus/`, one JSON file per game plus a README describing the record shape and the retirement rule copied from the fuzz corpus. `perf.rs` replays those inputs instead of dealing from the live pools; the heaviest-state selection then runs over the replayed games, so it stays deterministic too. Re-measure the medians once after pinning and keep the existing constants unless the pinned corpus moves them. Nothing about the budgets' meaning changes, and engine changes still move the timings (only the deals stop moving).

## Where it lands

- `crates/tools/src/perf.rs` (corpus construction; `crates/tools/README.md` perf row, enforced by `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs`)
- new `crates/tools/perf-corpus/` records and README (modelled on `crates/tools/fuzz-corpus/README.md`)
- `crates/tools/tests/perf.rs` (extend the corpus-shape assertions to the pinned files)
- No SPEC section: the budgets are CLAUDE.md rule 9 constants (`*_BUDGET_*` in `perf.rs`) measured under #3429.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Adding a card to the catalog (e.g. forcing an extra id into the fuzz pool) leaves every pinned corpus file byte-identical and `perf --smoke --json` reports the same corpus games.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test perf` passes, including a new assertion that each corpus game replays from its pinned file with no refused action.
- [ ] A corpus file holding a removed card id fails the lint with a message naming the `retired` marker to add, mirroring the fuzz corpus.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.

## Size and risks

Medium: about a hundred lines plus the corpus files. Risk is staleness if cards are removed (handled by the copied retirement rule) and the one-time re-measurement after pinning, which this issue's own acceptance run performs.

The engine-speed budgets the pull-request gate holds would stop wobbling every time cards ship.
